title: Tail-latency guardrails and concurrency planning (spreadsheet-first draft)
body:
Purpose

Capture a spreadsheet-driven approach for picking continuous-batching windows and provisioned concurrency targets that meet tail-latency SLOs (p95/p99), while minimizing GPU cost. This is a working doc intended to be translated into a shareable .xlsx with scenario tabs.

Audience
- Serving runtime team owners (sizing, scheduling)
- SRE and capacity planning
- Product owners for Dedicated commitments

Quick summary (TL;DR)
- Build a small set of canonical workload templates (chat short-turn, long-form generation, embedding heavy) with: arrival curve, token distribution, KV cache hit assumptions.
- For each template, compute required concurrency as a function of batching window and desired p95 latency using a queueing+service-time model in the spreadsheet.
- Translate concurrency -> GPU count via per-GPU sustained throughput model. Add safety margins for microbursts and KV-miss slowpaths.
- Derive cost per 1M tokens and per-1k-requests for each scenario, and surface breakpoints where switching quantization / model variant is cheaper than adding GPUs.

Assumptions (editable cells)
- arrival_rate_rps (requests/sec) default: 10
- tokens_requested_distribution: {"mean": 48, "p95": 256} (entered as two editable numbers)
- service_ms_per_token (baseline): 6 ms/token (FP16 medium model; editable)
- kv_cache_hit_rate: 0.45 default
- batching_window_ms options: [5, 15, 50, 100] (try each)
- queue_processing discipline: FIFO with batching aggregation
- allowed_p95_latency_ms target: 250 ms (configurable)

Core equations (represented as spreadsheet formulas)
- effective_service_time_ms = service_ms_per_token * expected_tokens_per_request * (1 + (1 - kv_cache_hit_rate) * extra_kv_miss_penalty_factor)
- average_batch_size = arrival_rate_rps * batching_window_ms / 1000 * cache_prefix_aggregation_factor
- per-request batching_delay_ms ≈ batching_window_ms / 2 (uniform arrival assumption) — NOTE: spreadsheet also includes a gamma-arrival tab for bursty arrivals
- mean_service_ms_per_request_in_batch = effective_service_time_ms / batch_parallelism_efficiency_factor
- observed_latency_ms ≈ batching_delay_ms + mean_service_ms_per_request_in_batch + scheduling_overhead_ms + network_rtt_ms
- p95_lat_factor_multiplier: empirical multiplier (default 1.6) to map mean-model latency -> p95; replace with measured distribution if available
- concurrency_needed = ceil((observed_rps * observed_mean_service_ms) / (1000 * per_worker_utilization_target))
- gpus_needed = ceil(concurrency_needed / threads_per_gpu)

Spreadsheet layout (recommended tabs)
- 00-README (notes / how to use)
- 01-templates (canonical workload templates and editable knobs)
- 02-queueing-core (formulas for batch sizing, delays, per-request latency decomposition)
- 03-simulated-arrivals (gamma/Poisson/microburst sims to compute p95 more realistically)
- 04-costs (map GPU hours -> $ cost, include reserved vs on-demand rates, discount tiers)
- 05-breakpoints (sensitivity grid: p95 target vs batching window -> cost surface)
- 06-experiments (actual run ids and measured results)

Worked example (numbers in-sheet, editable)
- Template: chat-short-turn
- arrival_rate_rps = 12
- mean_tokens = 28, p95_tokens = 120
- service_ms_per_token = 6
- kv_cache_hit_rate = 0.6, extra_kv_miss_penalty_factor = 0.5
- batching_window_ms = 15
- batching_delay_ms ≈ 7.5 ms
- expected_batch_size ≈ 12 * 0.015 = 0.18 -> because session-level aggregation reduces effective arrivals, we apply prefix_aggregation_factor = 3 -> average_batch_size ≈ 0.54 -> rounded up to batch of 1 (many small requests)
- effective_service_time_ms = 6 * 28 * (1 + (1 - 0.6) * 0.5) = 6 * 28 * 1.2 = 201.6 ms
- mean_service_in_batch_ms ≈ 201.6 / batch_parallelism_efficiency_factor (assume 1 for single-request batches) = 201.6 ms
- observed_latency ≈ 7.5 + 201.6 + 4 (sched+net) = 213 ms -> p95_estimate = 1.6 * 213 = 341 ms (misses 250 target)
- concurrency_needed: for observed 12 rps, concurrency = ceil((12 * 201.6) / (1000 * 0.7)) = ceil(2419.2 / 700) = ceil(3.456) = 4 concurrent workers
- threads_per_gpu = 12 -> gpus_needed = 1 (but add microburst safety -> 1.5 -> round up 2)
- cost implication: if GPU $3.2/hr, with 2 GPUs steady -> ~$1536/mo (730h) vs if we reduce model to faster variant (service_ms_per_token=4) then single GPU may suffice -> evaluate tradeoff in 05-breakpoints tab

Heuristics and guardrails (operational rules)
- If p95_est > target by > 15%: try 1) reduce batching_window (if safe), 2) increase concurrency (reserve capacity), 3) drop to smaller model variant or quantize.
- For microburst-prone workloads, prefer provisioning headroom >= 1.5x computed GPUs or implement burst-buffer allocation via Dedicated burst pool.
- Set per-customer soft-concurrency caps to prevent noisy neighbors from forcing global scaling.
- Use empirical p95 multipliers only as stopgaps; plan to replace them with sim-tab outputs or measured histograms.

Sensitivity experiments to run (spreadsheet-driven)
- Sweep batching_window_ms across [5, 10, 20, 50, 100] for each template and plot cost vs p95.
- Sweep kv_cache_hit_rate from 0.2 -> 0.9 to see model sensitivity to cache effectiveness.
- Sweep token_p95 and arrival burstiness (gamma shape k from 0.3 -> 10).
- Run headroom experiments for microburst frequency: add Poisson bursts of factor 3 for 200ms every N seconds and measure p95.

Data collection plan (to replace assumptions with measured values)
- Instrument per-request: tokens_requested, kv_cache_hit (bool), service_ms_per_token (time-series), batching_delay_ms, worker_id, GPU_utilization_samples
- Produce a per-workload histogram exporter: token_size_histogram, arrival_isi_histogram, service_time_histogram.
- Link simulation seeds to real-run ids (add to 06-experiments tab).

Open questions / TODOs
- How to capture multi-turn chat sessions that produce correlated arrivals (same session sends follow-up within short window)? spreadsheet has a naive prefix_aggregation_factor but we should replace with measured session-level autocorrelation coefficient.
- Determine a principled p95 multiplier mapping for wide range of burst shapes; current 1.6 is empirical from old A/B runs.
- Incorporate KV-miss cold-start penalty modeling for on-demand cold cache behavior (large variance).
- Decide on recommended safety headroom: 1.3x vs 1.5x vs 2x by workload criticality.

Action items (near-term)
- [Jordan] produce the initial .xlsx with the tab layout above and wire up example formulas (due: 2026-03-20).
- [Asha] run trace extraction job on 2026-02-01 -> 2026-02-28 traffic to populate 01-templates (due: 2026-03-10).
- [Diego] add a Poisson/gamma simulator sheet using sampled traces and provide p95 ground truths (due: 2026-03-18).
- [Rina] validate cost numbers (on-demand vs reserved) and add pricing matrix (due: 2026-03-12).

Notes for reviewers
- This doc intentionally keeps formulas high-level; spreadsheet will include explicit cell references and sensitivity charts.
- Expect several iterations after we replace multipliers with simulators and real telemetry.

References / links
- Confluence: CON-4567 (inference sizing patterns)
- Jira: JIRA-1234 (batching Q2 initiative)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/982 (scheduler microbatch change)

Version history
- 2025-11-02 initial draft by Jordan
- 2025-12-11 added example scenarios and heuristics (Asha)
- 2026-01-27 swapped in measured service_ms baseline from infra perf run
- 2026-02-28 updated action items and dates

Quick checklist before converting to final playbook
- [ ] Populate 01-templates with trace-derived templates
- [ ] Run sims and replace p95 multipliers with empirical percentiles
- [ ] Add GPU packing model (scheduling inefficiencies at >90% util)
- [ ] Review recommended headroom with SRE and Product

End.
